question: A 10-year-old girl falls and sustains an injury to her distal radius. Radiograph shows a fracture line entering the physis, traversing the epiphysis, and exiting through the articular surface. Which Salter-Harris type is this, and why does it carry the highest risk of growth disturbance among the fracture-line types?

answers.text: Salter-Harris II — because it is the most common type and crosses the metaphysis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SH II is the most common type (fracture through physis + metaphyseal fragment) but carries a relatively low risk of growth arrest. The description here — physis + epiphysis + articular surface — matches SH IV.

answers.text: Salter-Harris IV — because the fracture crosses both physis and epiphysis, risking physeal bar formation unless anatomically reduced

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. SH IV crosses the physis and the epiphysis, breaching both growth zones and the articular surface. Without exact anatomical reduction, a bony bridge (physeal bar) forms across the growth plate, causing angular deformity and limb-length discrepancy.

answers.text: Salter-Harris III — because it exits through the joint surface and risks avascular necrosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SH III fractures through the physis and exits through the epiphysis/articular surface but does not cross the metaphysis. The description here includes the fracture traversing the epiphysis from the physis — this matches SH IV not SH III.

answers.text: Salter-Harris V — because it crushes the germinal layer of the physis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SH V is a compression/crush injury with no fracture line on initial radiographs (often diagnosed retrospectively). The question describes a visible fracture line, which excludes SH V.

overallFeedback.feedback: SH IV: fracture line enters physis, crosses the epiphysis, exits articular surface. It requires ORIF to prevent physeal bar. Compare: SH III exits physis only through epiphysis (no metaphyseal component).
Correct. SH IV crosses physis + epiphysis → physeal bar risk → must reduce anatomically. Remember the mnemonic: SALTR (S=slip, A=above, L=lower, T=through, R=rammed/crush).
